scientific_queries.note: Annotation model versus a trivial marginal-mean baseline on GDSC.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round overturns the attribution of the programme's main positive result and rewrites the synthesis accordingly.

design.baseline: per-drug mean synergy from the training rows; pair score = mean of the two drug means; unseen drugs filled with the training median, i.e. ranked in the middle
settings: at least one drug unseen (~19,088-key pool)

attribution_change.before: C27/C41's decision value was attributed to the pathway-annotated ridge
attribution_change.after: the value is largely attributable to per-drug mean synergy; the annotation model adds no independent decision value, and on seen-drug pools its advantage over random is not even established (CI [-0.25,+3.75])
attribution_change.where_the_model_is_unique: only when both drugs are unseen, and there R66 measured just +1.25 pp with a CI lower bound of exactly 0

why_the_marginal_baseline_works_on_unsee: the any-unseen pool is mostly pairs with one seen and one unseen drug, so the marginal mean still carries information from the seen side
limits: the marginal-mean baseline is the one I constructed, not the best in the literature
unseen drugs are filled with the training median by design
the seen-pool ridge-minus-marginal CI still includes 0, so the correct statement is 'cannot claim the model is better', not 'the model is proven worse'
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: build a full marginal baseline (cell-side marginals plus drug x cell interactions) and compare it against the annotation model at the same budget
